top_story.headline: General Services Administration gives the Marine Corps' logistics contractor team a $92.6 million no-bid bridge while its replacement contract is competed
top_story.dek: The three-month bridge, with one three-month option, keeps the current supply chain contractors working while a new competition runs.
paragraphs: The General Services Administration posted a sole-source justification for a three-month bridge purchase agreement, with one three-month option, for fourth-party logistics (4PL) supply chain services at U.S. Marine Corps locations in the continental United States, Hawaii and Japan. The justification gives an estimated total value of $92,644,112. The vendor is the contractor team that already holds the current agreements: MSC Industrial Direct Co., Inc., L C Industries, Inc. and OSC Solutions, Inc.

Those current agreements (47QSCC21A0004, 0005 and 0006) were awarded under full and open competition, with a stated dollar value of $950,356,271 and a period of performance of July 26, 2021 to July 25, 2026. A six-month option extension runs to January 25, 2027. According to the justification, the bridge is needed during the acquisition phase of the replacement request for quotation, 47QSCC26Q5001, which the agency issued June 15, 2026.

The agency cites its schedule-ordering rules, which allow a sole-source order "in the interest of economy and efficiency because it is a logical follow-on to an FSS order already issued on a competitive basis." The justification is dated October 20, 2026, was posted today, and is redacted.

blocks.title: NASA adds sole-source spacesuit hardware to Axiom Space's Artemis contract through 2032, citing an executive order on returning to the Moon
meta: only one company can do it
National Aeronautics and Space Administration, Johnson Space Center
blocks.text: Axiom Space, Inc. holds NASA's xEVAS spacesuit services contract (80JSC022DA022), which is a service contract. The justification adds a supply line, CLIN 5, covering hardware production and delivery: development, upgrades, sustaining, maintenance, repair and refurbishment, running through May 30, 2032. It says the action "supports schedule resilience for Artemis consistent with national policy milestones set forth in Executive Order 14369," but adds that the order is cited "to document the schedule context only." No value is stated in the document. A second contractor, Collins Aerospace, was awarded a matching xEVAS contract on May 31, 2022.

blocks.title: Marine Corps posts a $262,726 sole-source award for Catholic priest services to an individual, Govindu Joseph
meta: Department of the Navy, Commanding General (Marine Corps)
blocks.text: The notice is titled "Intent to Sole Source Catholic Priest Services" (M6700127P1000) and was posted as an award notice naming Govindu Joseph as awardee. Only the notice blurb was available, with no justification document, so the stated reason for skipping competition is unknown. A religious-services purchase from an individual is an unusual buy for the Marine Corps.

sections.headline: Navy extends incumbent Virtual Computing Technology's squadron-support contract eight months while a GAO protest plays out
paragraphs: Three new extensions or bridges today. The largest, the $92.6 million Marine Corps logistics bridge from the General Services Administration, is today's Top Story and not repeated here.

blocks.title: Navy extends Virtual Computing Technology's squadron admin-support contract eight months without competition while protest corrective action continues
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
Naval Supply Systems Command, Fleet Logistics Center San Diego
blocks.text: The justification (J&A 27-240-0001) adds two option periods totaling eight months, a four-month base plus one four-month option, on a cost-plus-fixed-fee basis for Virtual Computing Technology, Inc. It provides administrative and personnel support to Fleet Replacement Squadrons, Air Test and Evaluation Squadrons and the two Navy air type-command headquarters. The Navy says the bridge maintains continuity while it completes corrective action on a protest filed with the Government Accountability Office on June 26, 2025, and covers time for any later protest. The document describes a "complex, multi-phased corrective action process following two GAO protests," and says the incumbent has 215 personnel already in place across 14 squadrons and two headquarters.

items: General Services Administration extends its office lease at REXCO Industrial Park in Guaynabo, Puerto Rico, without competition. The lease covers 4,048 rentable square feet and the value is redacted. (6PR0176)

sections.headline: Air Force tells vendors a classified SIPR or JWICS room can sit inside leased commercial office space near Hanscom

blocks.title: Air Force market research for leased office space near Hanscom says classified rooms can be built inside commercial buildings
blocks.text: The Air Force is surveying vendors for leased off-base commercial office space within 10 miles of Hanscom Air Force Base, Massachusetts. A question-and-answer file says "You do NOT strictly need a standalone building to host a SIPR room or JWICS access," because both can be built inside a multi-tenant facility as a "box-within-a-box" buildout.

footer.known_gaps: No source errors were reported. OMB Apportionments: no new apportionment files were approved between October 23 and October 28. Documents: 2,431 attachments on 473 notices were screened; 267 are access-restricted on SAM.gov, 1 could not be downloaded or read, and 1,602 are queued for a later edition (6,423 files overall are queued), so findings from them will come back as late document findings.
